text: The collapse of the ancient bridge serves as the inciting incident that drives the plot forward by isolating the villagers and forcing them to adapt. This event shifts the narrative from a state of dependence on the neighboring town to one of self-reliance, prompting the characters to find new paths and reconstruct their way of life. Consequently, the calamity acts as a catalyst for social change, uniting the community and fostering new leadership, which ultimately leads to the development of a more self-sufficient society.
